snippets.output: Antibiotics are effective in treating Lyme disease, particularly in the early stages of Lyme disease.
The primary goal of antibiotic treatment for Lyme disease is to eliminate the infection caused by Borrelia burgdorferi, the bacterium responsible for Lyme disease.

In the early stages of Lyme disease, antibiotics such as doxycycline and amoxicillin are commonly prescribed to prevent the progression of Lyme disease. Doxycycline and amoxicillin are antibiotics that work by targeting the bacteria and preventing the bacteria from reproducing and spreading.

If left untreated, Lyme disease can progress to later stages that may involve more severe symptoms such as arthritis, neurological problems, and heart issues. In these cases, treatment may involve longer courses of antibiotics and additional medications to manage symptoms.

Antibiotics are not effective against the late-stage symptoms of Lyme disease, such as arthritis or neurological problems, which are thought to be caused by the body's immune response to the infection. In these cases, treatment focuses on managing symptoms and alleviating discomfort.
